note: not to be confused with «сам», a form of бити (to be)
tips: Don't mix up the forms: «сам» - I am (урадио сам), «сам/сама» - alone, by oneself, and «само» - only. «Урадио сам то сам» - I did it myself.
«Сам сам» - I'm alone: the first is «alone», the second is «am» from бити. «Могу сама» - I can manage on my own. Само мало - just a second; само што нису стигли - they're about to arrive.

examples.en: The bus stopped in front of the school.

note: стало ми је до + gen. - I care about, ... matters to me

examples.en: This is the end of the movie.
In the end, I agreed anyway.

tips: In slang «крај» is the neighborhood where you live: «у мом крају» - in my neighborhood, «у крају» - somewhere nearby, in the area.

examples.en: Come as soon as you can.
I left my keys at home.
I've never seen such a house.

examples.sr: То је [у̏право] оно што ми треба.

tips: Exactly, precisely: «управо тај аутомобил желим», «управо сам разговарао са комшијом» - I was just talking to the neighbor.
It strengthens «exactly, precisely»: «управо тај аутомобил» - that very car. With the past tense it means «just now»: «управо сам разговарао».

examples.sr: Не свиђа ми се његов [на́чин] говора.
examples.en: I don't like his way of speaking.
The Earth revolves around the Sun.

tips: Country is земља or држава; «страна» means side or page.
Земља means earth (soil, the planet) and country: «страна земља» - a foreign country. Don't confuse it with «страна» (side) or «страница» (page).
Земљина кугла - the globe; Земљина оса, кора, језгро - the Earth's axis, crust, core. Земљиште - soil, ground, or a plot of land.

examples.en: Take an umbrella, just in case.
The police are investigating the case.
I booked a room at the hotel.

tips: Истина is the truth of a fact; «правда» means justice, fairness. «Жива истина» - the plain truth.

examples.en: This is the most beautiful part of the city.
I go to the gym once a week.

note: pl. браћа takes feminine singular agreement: моја браћа
tips: Брат is not only a biological brother: the word can be used for any male relative (uncle, cousins). Affectionately, a boy you don't know is «бато», a girl «сека».
The plural is the collective «браћа»: моја браћа, браћа су дошла.
The address «брате!» is closest to «bro» or «man»: friendly. Don't confuse it with «бре», a particle that only adds emotion.

examples.en: We're going downtown for a coffee.
Whatever you do, I'll love you.

note: ко год - whoever; шта год - whatever

forms: сећам се, сећају се; pf. сетити се
note: сећати се + gen.: сећам се тога
tips: Always with «се» and the genitive: «сећам се детињства», «сећам се тебе». Pf. pair - «сетити се» (to recall, to think of), impf. - to remember in general.
Takes the dative: «надати се нечему» (to hope for something). Common «надам се да...» - I hope that... The noun is «нада».

examples.en: I have a lot of work.

tips: After пуно comes the genitive: пуно воћа, пуно људи (not «пуно воће»). The same holds for мало, довољно, много.

examples.en: What are you trying to say?
We have to find a solution.
Cross to the other side of the street.
Open your books to page ten.

tips: Страна means both side and page: «с горње стране» - from above, «са стране» - from the side, «на све стране» - in all directions, «шалу на страну» - joking aside. Don't confuse it with «земља» (country).
Besides «side» it also means «page»: «на страни 10». The adjective «страни» means foreign: «страни језик».

examples.en: I want to become a doctor.
A lot of time has passed.
How did you do on the exam?

tips: «Проћи на испиту» - to pass an exam, «проћи на аудицији» - to get through an audition, «Добро си прошао!» - you got off easy, «прошло је лето» - summer is over.

examples.en: I'm leaving on a trip tomorrow.
I was in Greece last month.

tips: «Месец» is both a month (on the calendar) and the moon: «Мој омиљени месец је мај», «Месец је данас прелеп».

forms: свиђа ми се; pf. свидети се

examples.sr: Да ли ти се [сви̏ђа] моја хаљина?

note: the thing liked is the subject: свиђа ми се песма - I like the song
tips: Impf. - a state, a habit: «мени се свиђа овај град». Pf. «свидети се» - a moment: «свидео ми се ресторан», «свидеће ти се». The pronoun comes before the verb: «мени се свиђа».
The structure is reversed: the thing liked is the subject: «свиђаш ми се» - I like you (literally, you please me), «свидео си ми се», «свидело ми се». Synonym - «допадати се».
The thing liked is the subject, the person who likes is in the dative: Свиђаш ми се - I like you; Свиђа ми се песма - I like the song. Synonym: допадати се.

examples.en: Good deeds make the world a better place.

note: чини ми се - it seems to me
tips: «Чинити се» + dat. - «to seem»: «Чини ми се да је касно» - it seems to me that it's late; «чинило се немогућим» - it seemed impossible. Without «се» - simply «to do, to make».
Broader than «beautiful»: «лепа идеја» - a good idea, «леп мирис» - a pleasant smell, «лепа жена» - a beautiful woman, «хвала лепо» - thank you very much.
Not only «beautiful»: лепо време - fine weather, лепо мирише - smells nice, лепа реч - a kind word, леп посао - a good job, Лепо! - Great!

examples.sr: Таква несрећа може да се [до̀годи] свакоме.
examples.en: Such a misfortune can happen to anyone.
We've been living together for three years.
I haven't seen you for a long time.
Some guy was looking for you.
Put the book on the table.
Where did you put my phone?

tips: A very broad verb: put, place, add (шећер у кафу), apply (крему), put on (наочаре, минђуше), pose (питање). Impf. стављати.

For accessories instead of «обући»: ставити/скидати наочаре (glasses), шешир (hat), качкет (cap), минђуше (earrings), прстен (ring), сат (watch), шминку (makeup), крему (cream), кармин (lipstick), каиш (belt). «Ставити под кључ» - to lock up.
«Ставити кафу» - to put the coffee on (to brew it for a guest or oneself): «Ставићу кафу, седи». A common hospitable phrase.

examples.en: Do you want to go out tonight?

tips: «Реч» is a word («његове речи»); «слово» means a letter of the alphabet.
A speech or talk is «говор» or «обраћање».
Реч - «word»; a speech is говор, говор у јавности (public speaking).
Покушати да + present: «Покушаћу да дођем на време». «Немојте покушавати код куће!» - don't try this at home. «Покушај убиства» - attempted murder.

examples.en: I have quite a lot of work.
We were invited to a wedding.

tips: By phone: «Позовите ме сутра у 8» - call me tomorrow at 8. To call back - «узвратити позив» or «позвати касније»; to get through - «добити телефоном».

examples.en: We live in the same building.
The important thing is that you're alive.
Someone is knocking at the door.

note: plural only: ова врата су отворена - this door is open
tips: Always neuter plural, even for a single door: ова врата су дрвена, затвори врата.
Plural only: «door» is врата (n. pl.), «gate» is капија. With на: куцати на врата, на вратима. Collective numerals: једна врата, двоја врата, петора врата.

examples.sr: Драго ми је што смо се [упо̀знали].

examples.en: I want to introduce you to my parents.

tips: Takes the accusative: користим ову апликацију - I use this app.

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the post office?
I'll tell you the rest tomorrow.
We were walking toward the town.
He was very nice to me.
According to the forecast, it will rain tomorrow.
How far is it from here?
When did you last see him?
What are you carrying in your bag?
It's the struggle between good and evil.
I don't wish you any harm.

examples.sr: Било ми је [дра̑го] што сам те видео.
examples.en: I was glad to see you.

note: драго ми је - nice to meet you
tips: «Драго ми је!» is not only "nice to meet you": in reply to good news, or when a guest praises the meal («Баш ми је пријало!» - I really enjoyed that), it means "I'm so glad!"

examples.en: I spend weekends with my family.

note: фамилија means the extended «family», not a surname (that is презиме)
tips: Породица is the family in the narrow sense (mom, dad, me), «фамилија» is the wider circle: grandparents, aunts and uncles, cousins. «Фамилија» is not a «family name»: a surname is «презиме».

examples.sr: Можете ли ми [пока́зати] пут до станице?
examples.en: Could you show me the way to the station?
The cat is under the table.
He put the box under the bed.

note: also a noun «под» - floor: на поду

examples.en: I didn't manage to find him.

note: успети - to manage, to succeed; not «to be in time»
tips: Not «to make it in time» but «to manage, to succeed»: «успео сам да решим». For «to catch a train» you need the verb «стићи».
«Успети» - to work out, to manage; «Јеси ли успео?» - did you manage it? Not just «to make it in time».

examples.en: I'll be back in a couple of minutes.

examples.sr: Драго ми је што те [по̏ново] видим.
examples.en: I'm glad to see you again.
It's hard for me without you.
It's even harder for me now.

tips: It means «hard, difficult»: «Тешко ми је». Not «трудно»: «трудна» means pregnant.
More emotional than «па»: «Ма дај!», «Ма немој!», «Ма пусти то» - come on, no way, forget it. «Па не знам» - well, I don't know, «Ма не знам!» - how should I know?
An intensifier in dialogue: «Ма шта кажеш?» - what are you saying?!, «Ма иди!» - get out of here, no way!; «ма важи» - ironic: yeah, sure.
At the start of a reply, «come on, no way»: «Ма, свака част!» - hey, well done. It adds feeling and softens a refusal.

examples.en: What are we going to eat tonight?

tips: Past m.: «јео» (not «јел»), јела, јело, јели. Present: једем, једеш, једе, једемо, једете, једу.

examples.en: He was looking out the window.

tips: With time spans: кроз две недеље - in two weeks (in the future), кроз цео дан - through the whole day. Not for means: not «кроз стихове» but «стиховима»; not «кроз представнике» but «преко представника».
«Заиста» - really, actually: «заиста не знам» - I really don't know; in a question: «да ли заиста мислиш тако?».

examples.en: I'm not at home at the moment.
Tonight we're going to the theater.

tips: Time words: вечерас (this evening), јутрос (this morning), ноћас (tonight), синоћ (last night). Not «данас увече».

examples.en: Thank you from the bottom of my heart.
He wrote her letters full of love.

tips: «With love» is «с љубављу»: the instrumental of a feminine noun ending in a consonant takes -ју.

examples.en: I'll stay for a few days.
Do you want to play cards?

note: играти + acc. without a preposition: играти шах; also «to dance»
tips: Games and sports take the accusative with no preposition: играм тенис, играмо фудбал. For a musical instrument use свирати: свирам гитару.

examples.en: After his death she moved away.
On Sunday we're going to grandma's.

tips: It means both «Sunday» and «week»: «данас је недеља» - today is Sunday; «за недељу дана» - in a week. The meaning is clear from context.
A seven-day week is both «недеља» and «седмица». «Седмица» has only this meaning, so people often say «сваке седмице» (every week) to avoid confusion with Sunday.
«Недељом» - on Sundays (like «понедељком», «суботом»). «Сваке недеље» means every week or every Sunday, depending on context.

examples.en: What shoe size do you wear?

tips: Besides «number» («број телефона») it also means a size of clothing or shoes: «Имате ли већи број?» Physical dimensions are «димензије».
Besides number, figure - also a shoe size: «ципеле без броја» - shoes without a size (from a children's song). Also «бројити» - to count.
Also a number and a shoe or clothing size: «Треба ми број 37» - I need a size 37. What size do you wear? - Који број носите?

examples.en: I have to go to the doctor.
It can't go on like this.
I'll be there in five minutes.

tips: Masculine: минут (pl. минути, but after 2-4 «минута»): један минут, пет минута.

examples.en: My sister lives in Novi Sad.

tips: A cry for help: «У помоћ!». In Serbia: ambulance 194, police 192, fire brigade 193, roadside assistance 1987.

examples.en: That's not a very good idea.
What should I buy for dinner?

examples.sr: Да ли си [схва̀тила] шта сам рекао?
examples.en: Did you understand what I said?

tips: Схватити means «to understand» (ја сам схватио), not to grab physically: that is «ухватити, зграбити».
Правити - to create something material («правим торту»); радити - to do work («радим домаћи»); чинити - to do deeds («чиниш добро дело»).
Правити = to make, prepare: кафу, ручак, колаче, буку, проблеме. «Правити се + adj.» - to pretend: правити се луд, паметан. «Правити слику» - to take a picture.

examples.en: Where did you park the car?
How did you find that out?
I want to find out the truth.

tips: Pf. of «знати»: to find out, learn something new: «сазнао сам где је библиотека». «Знам где је» - I know where it is in general, I'm already aware.

examples.en: After lunch we go for a walk.
He came back after two years.

note: colloq.; both a greeting and a farewell

examples.en: The ship is sailing down the Danube.

tips: Брод is a ship, a vessel: «трговачки брод» - a merchant ship. The nave of a church is also «брод». A ford (a shallow river crossing) is «газ».

note: of people: познајем га - I know him

tips: «Из тог разлога» - for that reason, «из ког разлога» - for what reason. Don't confuse it with «разлаз» (parting, divergence).

examples.en: I arrived at eight o'clock sharp.
A beautiful painting hangs on the wall.

related.en: to paint, to draw; to photograph

examples.en: We have no chance at all.

tips: «Шанса» is feminine: добра шанса.

note: feminine, also of a man: он је добра особа
tips: «Особа» is used for qualities: оптимистична особа (an optimistic person), rather than «оптимистичан човек».

examples.en: Wash your face with cold water.

examples.sr: Видео сам му на [ли̑цу] да лаже.
examples.en: I could see from his face that he was lying.
I waited for more than an hour.

tips: «Преко реда» - out of turn, cutting in line: «Не може преко реда!» - no cutting in line.
Colloquially «преко» also means abroad: отићи преко - to go abroad to work or live.

examples.en: The taxi driver took us to the airport.
Look after the kids until I get there.

note: пазити на + acc. - to look after
tips: Пазите! - careful!; пазити на + acc. - to take care of, look after someone or something (на децу, на ствари).

examples.en: I won't make it on time.

tips: To arrive, to get there: «стићи кући», «стићи на време». Also «стићи» + infinitive - to have time to: «нисам стигао да погледам».
Also «to make it in time» («не стижем» - I can't make it, «стигао сам на воз» - I made the train) and «to catch up with» («не могу да га стигнем»). «To be in time» can only be said with «стићи».
Стићи also means «to have time to»: «Нисам стигао да вечерам» - I didn't have time to eat dinner. Impf. - «стизати».

examples.en: So, what do we do now?

tips: «Платити» is broader than the English «to pay»: to pay for something, pay off, repay, compensate: «платити дуг» (pay a debt), «платити казну» (pay a fine).

examples.en: What's the plan for the weekend?
He always returns books on time.
My younger brother goes to school.
It's easy for you to talk.

tips: Бар / барем - «at least, at a minimum»: «треба ми бар пет минута». The intensifier «чак» - «as many as, even»: «попио је чак три чаше».
The variant «барем» (at least) is the same, both words are equal. Close in meaning: «макар», «најмање» (at the very least), «у најмању руку».

examples.en: They named their son after his grandfather.
Follow me, I know the way.

tips: Not only «to follow»: пратити моду, пратити некога = to follow someone, to be subscribed to them. The object is in the accusative without a preposition: не пратим моду.
A broad word: to accompany (пратити до школе), to follow the news, and on social media - to follow: пратим те на инстаграму.
Запратити - to start following on social media; «пратити причу» - to follow a story; «пратити своје срце» - to follow your heart. Don't confuse it with «прати» (to wash).
In conversation it can be a compliment: «луд си!» - you're wild, you're awesome.
«Луд за + instr.» - crazy about something: «Она је луда за музиком».

examples.en: I wish you lots of happiness!

tips: One word for both «happiness» and «luck»: «имати среће» - to be lucky, «срећно!» - good luck. From it comes «срећка» - a lottery ticket; the slogan «Огреби срећу!» is a play on words.
One word for both happiness and luck: «Срећа је да смо отишли на време» - it's lucky we left in time. «Срећом» - luckily, «несрећа» - misfortune, accident.
«Срећа» - happiness and luck: «Имам среће» - I'm lucky, «Немам среће» - I'm out of luck, «Срећа прати храбре» - fortune favors the brave.

examples.en: There were two men in the room.
I gave blood at the hospital.
I was by your side all the time.

tips: Besides «with»: next to (уз прозор), up (уз брдо), accompanied by (уз музику), with the help of (уз помоћ), as an accompaniment to a dish or an outfit, support. Always + acc.

note: бојати се + gen.: бојим се мрака
tips: After бојати се comes the genitive: бојим се мрака, воде, висине (afraid of the dark, water, heights). The particle се stays next to the verb: Не бојим се змија.

examples.en: I need to tidy up the room.
Don't worry, I'll sort it out.

tips: To put in order: «средити папире», «средити ормар». The opposite is пореметити, to disrupt the order.
«Средити се» - to get oneself together, to be transformed: «баш си се средила!» - what a transformation (you look great).
The difference is in the means: «довести» - to bring (leading on foot), «довезти» - to bring by vehicle. Impf.: «доводити» / «довозити».

examples.en: My grandfather was in the war.

tips: Рат за независност - war of independence, ослободилачки рат - war of liberation, крсташки рат - crusade, грађански рат - civil war.

examples.en: What does it say in that book?
I'm writing a letter to my mom.

note: шта пише? - what does it say?
tips: The past tense of «писати» is built from the infinitive stem: «писао/писала». The form «пишао» belongs to another verb, пишати (to pee, colloq.). Don't mix them up.

examples.en: Check whether the door is locked.
I need to check my mail.

examples.sr: Мој [са̏н] је да путујем по свету.
examples.en: My dream is to travel the world.

tips: As a noun, «dream» in the sense of an ambition is «сан»: «Сан ми се остварио» - my dream came true. «Машта» (imagination) does not work for this.

examples.en: Why are you standing? Sit down.
The car is parked in front of the house.

tips: Also «to keep, not go bad»: «Малине дуго не стоје» - raspberries don't keep long.
The verb's stem changes: стајати - стојим, стоје (the suffix «-а-» becomes «-о-»). «Стајати» - to stand, and also to suit, of clothes: «лепо ти стоји».

examples.en: Her husband works as a doctor.
The ship's captain is an experienced sailor.
Bring me a glass of water.
We have a dog and a cat.
The neighbor's dog barks all night.

tips: A homonym: пас - a dog (gen. «пса») and a belt («пас око струка»).
An adult dog - «пас» (имам пса, немам пса; the accusative equals the genitive for animate nouns), a puppy - «штене»/«куче», affectionately - «куца».
Kinds of dogs: пас луталица - stray dog, ловачки пас - hunting dog, пас чувар - guard dog. Пас is the neutral word; куче - puppy, куца - affectionate, кер - mutt, pejorative.

examples.en: I ate half of the pizza.

examples.sr: У овом [фѝлму] глуми мој омиљени глумац.
examples.en: My favorite actor stars in this movie.

tips: The adjective филмски: филмска уметност (cinematography), филмски фестивал, филмска пројекција (film screening), филмска екипа (film crew). A cartoon - цртани филм.

examples.en: I've been thinking about your offer.
Mrs. Jovanović is waiting for you.
I learned Serbian in a year.

examples.sr: Био је уморан, али је [и̏па̄к] отишао.
examples.en: He was tired, but he went all the same.
The dog ran away from the yard.
You can't run away from the truth.
Do you know how to drive?
I drive the kids to school.

note: возити се - to ride: возим се аутобусом
tips: «Возим аутобус» - I'm a bus driver; «возим се аутобусом» - I'm riding a bus as a passenger. Without «се» the meaning is different!

examples.en: I talked to him on the phone.

tips: The stress falls on the second syllable: теле́фон (English puts it on the first).
Pf. - «слагати» (to tell a lie): «слагала сам га» - I lied to him. Don't confuse it with «слагати» (to fold, put together) and «слагати се» (to agree).

examples.en: We have no food in the fridge.

tips: Храна is ordinary food, the neutral word. «Нафака» is bookish, of Turkish origin: sustenance as one's share allotted by fate; you don't buy «нафака» at a market.

examples.en: The car is behind the house.
I can't be bothered to get up.

note: мрзи ме - I can't be bothered

examples.en: Let me know when you arrive.

examples.sr: Звао сам те, што се ниси [ја̏вио]?
examples.en: I called you, why didn't you answer?

note: јавити се - to pick up the phone; to get in touch
tips: «Јавити се» - to get in touch, including by phone: «Јавићу ти се сутра» - I'll get in touch tomorrow. Impf. «јављати се».
With «се»: to answer a call or in class, to get in touch («јавићу ти се сутра»), to respond to a job ad, to make itself felt («јавио ми се бол у леђима» - back pain showed up).
Јавити се - to make contact, to say hello or goodbye: «Јави ми се!» - call me, let me know; «Морам да се јавим Драгани» - I have to get in touch with Dragana. Impf. - јављати.
With a number «скоро» means «almost»: «скоро 50 година». Age is expressed with «имати»: «имам скоро 50 година», not «ја сам 50».

examples.en: Leave a message after the tone.
He doesn't have a license for the weapon.
I leave the house at eight.
They've been dating for a year.
I sit at the computer all day.
I need to ask the boss.
